transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Fitzgerald. I am Dr. Miller. I know you've already spoken with the nurse about what happened, but I wanted to come and talk to you directly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't know. She told me something was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so sorry. We made a mistake in how we read your grandchild's heart rate tracing. I was the doctor who reviewed it, and I categorized the heart rate patterns incorrectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? How can you make a mistake with a baby?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in my judgment during the review. The tracing showed decelerations, which means the baby's heart rate was dropping, but I didn't recognize the severity of those drops at the time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My husband... Arthur would have known what to do. He was always the one who handled the doctors. I feel so alone in this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed and missing Arthur's support right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am. I just can't believe this is happening. Was the baby hurt?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure I'm being clear about the error. The heart rate drops were missed for two hours before a second doctor reviewed the trace and identified the true severity. Does that make sense, or can I explain that part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I understand. You just didn't see it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. I missed it. I take full responsibility for that error. There is no excuse for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two hours... two hours where nothing was being done. It's just... I can't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is incredibly frightening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He would be so angry. Arthur would be furious that you just ignored it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you would feel that way. I am truly sorry for the distress this has caused you and your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Is the baby okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure we have a clear path forward, here is the plan. First, the neonatal team is going to perform a full physical assessment and a blood gas check within the next thirty minutes to ensure the baby has recovered fully.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: After that, the consultant will meet with you here at 4:00 PM today to review those results and discuss the long-term follow-up. Your role right now is to let us know if you notice any changes in how the baby is feeding or breathing. Does that timeline work for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose. I just don't know if I can trust you people.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand why your trust is shaken. To prevent this from happening again, I am reporting this incident to our quality board today, and we are implementing a mandatory second-signature requirement for all high-risk tracings starting tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want the baby to be alright.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. Now, I really need to go check on the latest readings in the nursery, but I will come back to check on you before the consultant arrives.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, you're leaving? I still feel like I'm floating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be right back, I just need to verify the latest stats.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just so much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that. I'll be back in ten minutes. Just to be sure we're on the same page, do you have any other questions about the error itself before I step out for a moment?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I just... I just wish Arthur were here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you're going through this without him. I'll see you very shortly.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language when attempting to leave the room ('I really need to go', 'I'll be right back, I just need to verify').

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense', 'do you have any other questions').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language, takes full personal responsibility ('I missed it'), and maintains this under pushback regarding the two-hour delay.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed', 'frightening') and engages the patient's emotional bids regarding her late husband Arthur.

T.justification: The resident provides specific steps with timelines (30 mins, 4:00 PM), defines the patient's role (monitoring feeding/breathing), and addresses prevention (quality board/second-signature).
